ref: Annex I, Part I, point (1); Art 13(1), Art 13(2)
title: Secure-by-Design & Risk-Based Engineering Lifecycle
description: Products with digital elements shall be designed, developed, and produced in such a way that they ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks identified in the manufacturer's cybersecurity risk assessment.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all products with digital elements without exception)
stakeholder: Lead Security Architect, Systems Engineer, CISO
guidance: Incorporate threat modelling, secure architecture reviews, and risk assessment into early concept and architecture phases. Security requirements must directly derive from identified threat scenarios (STRIDE/PASTA/IEC 62443). Risk assessment must be updated iteratively as architecture evolves.
controls: Organizational Secure SDLC policy; mandatory threat modeling gates at design review; architectural risk register; security architecture review board sign-off prior to code development.
evidence: Formal Threat Model Document; Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Report (Annex VII Dossier); System Architecture Security Specification; Architectural Gate Review Sign-off.
criteria: All identified threat vectors have mapped, documented security mitigations; residual cybersecurity risk is formally signed off by Lead Architect and CISO as acceptable.
limitations: Automated code scanners and vulnerability tools cannot evaluate high-level architecture, threat models, or design intent. Threat Analysis and Risk Analysis (TARA) provides the primary analytical framework.
additional_controls: Formal Threat Modeling process (STRIDE/PASTA); Secure Architecture Review Board; Risk Assessment Methodology aligned with ISO/IEC 27005 / IEC 62443-4-1.
notes: Foundational requirement underpinning all other Annex I controls. Must be documented in the Annex VII Technical Documentation Dossier.

ref: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(a); Art 3(41)
title: Absence of Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities at Placement
description: Products with digital elements shall be delivered without any known exploitable vulnerabilities at the time of placing on the market.
applicability: Mandatory (Strict liability condition at the moment of market placement)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Lead Security Architect, Release Manager
guidance: Implement automated CI/CD gating breaking builds on Critical/High vulnerabilities in custom code or third-party dependencies. Where a known CVE cannot be patched prior to release, conduct a formal VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) analysis proving non-exploitability in product context.
controls: Automated SAST/SCA build quality gates; pre-release penetration testing; automated container/OS scanning; formal VEX assessment process (CSAF/CycloneDX VEX) for justified false positives/unexploitable CVEs.
evidence: Pre-release SAST scan reports; SCA dependency scan reports; Penetration test final report; Signed VEX Declaration; Release Gate Approval Record.
criteria: Zero unresolved Critical/High vulnerabilities without documented, validated 'none_affected' / 'not_exploitable' VEX status; clean penetration testing validation.
limitations: Scanners detect potential vulnerabilities based on signatures/rules; only manual Penetration Testing and contextual VEX analysis can verify real-world exploitability in the integrated environment.
additional_controls: Contextual VEX triage board; formal release gating policy; vulnerability waiver process signed by Product Security Officer.
notes: Under Art 3(41), 'exploit' means the capability to breach cybersecurity. Even if upstream CVE exists, if execution path is unreachable, VEX must substantiate this for compliance audit.

title: Secure Default Configuration & Factory Reset Capability
description: Products with digital elements shall be delivered with a secure default configuration, including the possibility to reset the product to its original state, and ensuring that users are protected against insecure configurations.
applicability: Mandatory (Default); Conditional (May be tailored for custom enterprise B2B solutions upon explicit contractual agreement under Recital 64)
stakeholder: System Architect, Product Engineering Lead, Technical Writer
guidance: Enforce secure-by-default parameters: disable insecure legacy protocols (Telnet, HTTP, SMBv1), enforce unique random passwords per device (no default admin/admin), require password changes on first boot, and provide a verified factory reset mechanism that wipes user data while restoring secure baselines.
controls: CIS Benchmark / DISA STIG hardening scripts; automated configuration compliance auditing; cryptographically secured factory reset utility; forced password change on first setup.
evidence: CIS Benchmark Configuration Compliance Audit Report; Hardening Specification Document; Factory Reset Verification Test Record; User Manual Secure Configuration Guide (Annex II).
criteria: Default installation passes CIS benchmark with zero high-risk deviations; unique per-device credentials verified; factory reset reliably restores hardened baseline and scrubs credentials.
limitations: Code-level SAST and SCA cannot assess deployed system configurations, daemon settings, or reset mechanics. Nessus/Cyberwatch directly audits OS/service hardening against CIS benchmarks.
additional_controls: Automated OS/firmware hardening automation (Ansible/Puppet); physical/logical reset button testing; user installation guide gating.
notes: Recital 64 allows tailor-made bespoke B2B software to negotiate specific configuration defaults with customers, provided the waiver is formally documented in the contract.

ref: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(c); Annex I, Part II, point (7)
title: Automatic Security Updates by Default with User Notification
description: Products with digital elements shall ensure that security updates are delivered automatically by default where technically feasible, with clear user notifications and opt-out capabilities.
applicability: Mandatory (Where technically feasible; conditional exemption for OT/industrial safety systems where unexpected restarts create operational hazards)
stakeholder: Firmware / Platform Architect, Release Engineering Lead, Product Manager
guidance: Implement an automated background update mechanism for security patches. Users must receive clear notifications prior to/after installation, have an easy opt-out toggle in UI/CLI, and have the ability to defer reboots. Security patches must be separated from functional updates.
controls: OTA / background update daemon with dual-partition A/B rollback protection; cryptographic signature verification of update packages; update scheduling and user notification UI; opt-out preference persistence.
evidence: Update Architecture Specification; Automated Update Mechanism Test Report; Rollback & Anti-Downgrade Test Record; Annex II User Instructions on Update Configuration.
criteria: Automated update installs successfully in test environments; invalid/corrupt updates automatically trigger rollback; opt-out setting successfully defers automated deployment.
limitations: Security scanning tools do not build or test update delivery mechanics. Penetration testing can evaluate rollback resistance and signature verification bypasses.
additional_controls: OTA update infrastructure; code-signing HSM integration; update daemon resilience testing; customer operational release runbook.
notes: For critical infrastructure or OT devices where automatic updates violate safety standards (e.g. IEC 61508), manufacturers must provide clear justification in Annex VII technical documentation.

title: Protection Against Unauthorized Access & Identity Management
description: Products with digital elements shall ensure protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms, including authentication, identity or access management systems, and report on possible unauthorised access.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all products with user, administrative, or machine-to-machine interfaces)
stakeholder: Lead Software Architect, DevSecOps Lead, IAM Specialist
guidance: Implement robust authentication (MFA for administrative interfaces, API key/mTLS for machine interfaces), fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC/ABAC), secure session management (short-lived tokens, secure cookies), rate limiting on authentication endpoints, and brute-force lockout mechanisms.
controls: Centralized IAM framework (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / SAML); PBKDF2/Argon2/bcrypt password hashing; mTLS for internal service meshes; account lockout policies; RBAC enforcement on all API routes.
evidence: IAM Architecture Design Document; RBAC Matrix; Authentication Unit & Integration Test Suites; Penetration Testing Report (Auth/Privilege Escalation); DAST Scan Report.
criteria: Zero unauthorized access bypasses in penetration tests; MFA enforced on administrative paths; session tokens cryptographically random with secure flags; brute-force attacks mitigated.
limitations: SonarQube/Coverity can detect hardcoded credentials and basic session flaws in code. DAST (OWASP ZAP/Burp) and Penetration Testing provide primary direct validation of runtime authentication/authorization logic.
additional_controls: Automated API fuzzing for IDOR/BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization); credential stuffing defenses; periodic identity posture audits.
notes: Covers both human user accounts and automated API / service accounts connecting to or within the PDE and associated Remote Data Processing Solutions (RDPS).

title: Data Confidentiality Protection via State-of-the-Art Cryptography
description: Products with digital elements shall protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data, personal or other, such as by encrypting relevant data at rest or in transit by state of the art mechanisms.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all sensitive, credential, telemetry, and personal data processed by the product)
stakeholder: Security Architect, Cryptographic Engineer, Backend Developer
guidance: Enforce TLS 1.3 (or strictly configured TLS 1.2 with PFS ciphers) for all data in transit. Enforce AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, or equivalent modern authenticated encryption for data at rest. Securely manage cryptographic keys using KMS/HSM/TPM; never hardcode keys in source code.
controls: Standard cryptographic libraries (OpenSSL FIPS, BouncyCastle, libsodium); automated secret scanning in Git/CI; TLS enforcement proxies; transparent database encryption (TDE) or volume encryption.
evidence: Cryptographic Architecture & Key Management Plan; TLS Configuration Audit Report (SSLLabs / Nessus); SAST Secret & Crypto Scan Reports; Static Analysis Crypto API Audit.
criteria: No deprecated ciphers (RC4, 3DES, MD5, SHA1, ECB mode) present; zero plaintext transmissions; keys stored outside codebase in HSM/secret vault; automated scans confirm strong crypto.
limitations: SonarQube and Coverity detect weak crypto algorithms and hardcoded secrets in code; Nessus verifies TLS cipher suites in runtime. Cryptographic key lifecycle management requires architectural policies.
additional_controls: Key Management System (KMS) governance; automated Secret Scanner (TruffleHog/GitGuardian); Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) tracking.
notes: Alignment with ENISA guidance on cryptographic algorithms and key sizes is strongly recommended to substantiate 'state of the art' legal threshold.

title: Data & Execution Integrity Protection
description: Products with digital elements shall protect the integrity of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data, personal or other, commands, programs and configuration against manipulation or tampering.
applicability: Mandatory (All critical data streams, firmware images, system files, and command channels)
stakeholder: Lead Software Architect, DevSecOps Lead, Systems Engineer
guidance: Implement cryptographic signatures (ECDSA/RSA) for firmware, configuration files, and software updates. Use secure boot mechanisms (UEFI Secure Boot, hardware root of trust). Protect API requests against tampering using HMAC, digital signatures, or TLS integrity. Implement memory safety controls against memory corruption tampering.
controls: Code signing in CI/CD pipeline using hardware HSM; Secure Boot verification; File Integrity Monitoring (FIM); HMAC message authentication; parameterized queries and input validation preventing memory/state corruption.
evidence: Secure Boot & Code Signing Verification Spec; CI/CD Artifact Signing Logs; File Integrity Monitoring Baseline; Pentest Tampering Assessment Report.
criteria: System rejects unsigned/tampered binaries and updates; memory corruption attacks cannot overwrite execution flow; API rejects tampered parameters; FIM alerts on unauthorized configuration changes.
limitations: SAST (Coverity/SonarQube) detects unsafe memory manipulation and deserialization in code. Penetration testing tests data tampering and command injection in transit. HSM code-signing requires infrastructure controls.
additional_controls: Enterprise Code Signing Infrastructure; Sigstore / Cosign container signing; Hardware Security Module (HSM) key protection; SLSA build level verification.
notes: Covers both data at rest/transit and the execution runtime environment to prevent malicious code injection and binary modification.

title: Data Minimisation & Processing Proportionality
description: Products with digital elements shall process only data, personal or other, that are adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the intended purpose of the product.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all data collection, telemetry, analytics, and operational logging)
stakeholder: Data Protection Officer (DPO), Product Manager, Lead Architect
guidance: Apply privacy-by-design and data minimisation principles across all features. Remove unnecessary telemetry collection; anonymize/pseudonymize diagnostic data; provide user controls to disable telemetry; establish automated data retention and pruning schedules.
controls: Data flow mapping; DPIA execution; configurable telemetry opt-out switches; automated database purge jobs; schema reviews preventing excessive field capture.
evidence: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) Report; Data Inventory and Processing Register (GDPR Art 30 / CRA); Telemetry Configuration Architecture; Privacy Policy / Annex II Disclosure.
criteria: DPIA approved by DPO; no unneeded personal or sensitive data ingested; telemetry collection strictly opt-in or easily disabled; automated data purging verified.
limitations: Technical vulnerability scanners have zero capability to assess legal data minimization or processing necessity. The DPIA process directly and specifically addresses this legal requirement.
additional_controls: Formal GDPR Art 35 DPIA process; Product Privacy Review Gate; Telemetry opt-out UX validation.
notes: Extends beyond GDPR personal data to cover any non-personal data where excessive collection increases cyberattack blast radius.

title: Essential Function Availability & Denial-of-Service Resilience
description: Products with digital elements shall protect the availability of essential functions, including resilience against and mitigation of denial-of-service attacks.
applicability: Mandatory (Critical for products providing operational or network services)
stakeholder: Infrastructure Architect, Lead Backend Engineer, Network Engineer
guidance: Architect system with graceful degradation and circuit breakers. Implement rate limiting on APIs, resource quotas (CPU, memory, file descriptors, connection limits), request size caps, and anti-amplification controls. For cloud/RDPS backends, deploy DDoS mitigation (CDN, WAF, autoscaling).
controls: API gateway rate limiting (Token Bucket / Leaky Bucket); ingress request throttling; WAF DDoS protection rules; resource cgroups / container quotas; connection timeout configurations; algorithmic ReDoS protections.
evidence: High Availability & DoS Resilience Architecture Spec; Stress / Load / DoS Simulation Test Report; Penetration Test DoS Resistance Assessment; Cloud WAF Configuration.
criteria: System maintains essential services under sustained simulated traffic spikes/attacks; rate-limiting drops excessive requests without crashing backends; no algorithmic ReDoS crashes.
limitations: SAST tools detect algorithmic complexity flaws (ReDoS) or resource leaks in code; Nessus identifies known DoS CVEs in services. Penetration testing and automated stress testing provide primary empirical verification.
additional_controls: Automated Chaos Engineering / DDoS simulation testing; CDN/WAF DDoS mitigation infrastructure; rate-limiting integration tests.
notes: Essential functions must be explicitly defined in the Annex VII technical documentation and categorized according to failure impact.

title: Minimisation of Impact on External Networks & Connected Devices
description: Products with digital elements shall minimise the negative impact by the products themselves or connected devices on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks.
applicability: Mandatory (Critical for networked devices, IoT endpoints, and client software)
stakeholder: Network Architect, Systems Engineer, Firmware Developer
guidance: Prevent product from being weaponized as a botnet node, DDoS reflector, or network flood amplifier. Disable open DNS resolvers, NTP amplification, UPnP, and open proxying. Implement egress filtering, outbound connection rate limiting, and exponential backoff on retries.
controls: Outbound connection rate limiting; disabling reflection/amplification protocols; DNS request throttling; strict egress firewall rules; jittered exponential backoff on connection retries.
evidence: Network Protocol & Egress Control Specification; Network Traffic Flood / Amplification Test Report; Penetration Test Network Abuse Assessment.
criteria: Product cannot be coerced into generating amplified reflection traffic; outbound retry storms throttled during network outages; no open relay or proxy behavior.
limitations: Nessus scans identify open amplification protocols (DNS, NTP, SNMP, UPnP). Penetration testing and DAST (Burp) test for SSRF and outbound proxy abuse.
additional_controls: Network abuse prevention testing; egress traffic filtering verification; outbound retry circuit breakers.
notes: Designed to prevent widespread Mirai-style IoT botnet recruitment and cascading infrastructure disruption across the EU digital single market.

title: Attack Surface Reduction & Interface Pruning
description: Products with digital elements shall be designed, developed and produced to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces, to what is strictly necessary.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all software, hardware, and network interfaces)
stakeholder: Lead Security Architect, Systems Engineer, Embedded/Platform Lead
guidance: Identify and eliminate unused network ports, background services, APIs, debug interfaces (JTAG, UART, SSH/telnet debug shells), and unneeded software packages. Apply minimal OS images (Distroless, Alpine, minimal Yocto builds). Expose only documented endpoints required for intended functionality.
controls: Port lockdown and firewalling; removal of debug tools/symbols from production builds; minimal base container images; API gateway endpoint whitelisting; dead code pruning.
evidence: Interface & Port Inventory Document; Port Scan Audit Report (Nessus/Nmap); Build Pipeline Hardening Spec (Debug Symbol Stripping); Penetration Test Attack Surface Assessment.
criteria: Only explicitly justified ports open in production builds; debug interfaces physically/logically disabled; minimal container attack surface verified by scanner.
limitations: Threat Modeling (TARA) establishes the architectural attack surface baseline; Nessus directly audits running network ports and services; Black Duck/Nexus identify unused dependency bloat.
additional_controls: Continuous port scanning in staging/production; container base image slimming; CI build compiler flag enforcement (`-O2 -s`).
notes: Must document all exposed external interfaces and communication protocols in the Annex VII Technical Documentation Dossier.

title: Software Exploitation Mitigation Techniques
description: Products with digital elements shall be designed, developed and produced to reduce the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation mitigation techniques and mechanisms.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all compiled code, runtime execution environments, and containers)
stakeholder: Platform Architect, DevSecOps Lead, Senior Software Engineer
guidance: Enforce modern compiler exploit mitigations: ASLR (Address Space Layout Randomization), DEP/NX (Data Execution Prevention), Stack Canaries (`-fstack-protector-strong`), Safe Stack, RELRO (Relocation Read-Only), and CFI (Control Flow Integrity). Use memory-safe programming languages (Rust, Go, Python, modern Java) where feasible. Enforce sandboxing and container isolation (seccomp, AppArmor).
controls: Compiler security hardening flags in CI/CD toolchain; memory safety linters and deep static analysis; container sandboxing (read-only rootfs, unprivileged user, dropped capabilities); SELinux/AppArmor profiles.
evidence: Compiler Security Flags Verification Report (`checksec` output); Coverity Deep Static Analysis Memory Safety Report; Container Security Runtime Baseline; Pentest Exploit Mitigation Validation.
criteria: `checksec` confirms full RELRO, Canary, NX, and PIE on all compiled binaries; Coverity detects zero critical memory corruption/buffer overflow defects; containers run unprivileged with read-only filesystems.
limitations: Coverity is the premier deep static analyzer for detecting complex memory corruption, pointer arithmetic, and concurrency flaws in C/C++/Java. `checksec` / binary linters verify compiler mitigations in the CI pipeline.
additional_controls: Automated binary analysis with `checksec` in release pipeline; memory-safe language adoption roadmap; hardened runtime execution profiles.
notes: Essential requirement targeting the mitigation of zero-day exploits and memory safety vulnerabilities.

title: Security-Relevant Event Logging & Audit Monitoring
description: Products with digital elements shall record and store relevant internal activity related to cybersecurity, including the logging of events, and provide the possibility for the user to access and delete the logs, with opt-out mechanisms where appropriate.
applicability: Mandatory (Security logging is mandatory; user opt-out and deletion apply to non-essential diagnostic/activity logs without compromising core audit integrity)
stakeholder: Security Engineer, Platform Architect, Operations / SRE Lead
guidance: Implement standardized audit logging for authentication events, privilege changes, administrative actions, access control denials, and system configuration modifications. Ensure logs are tamper-resistant, timestamped (NTP synchronized), and do not record sensitive data (passwords, encryption keys, PII). Provide export capabilities (Syslog/SIEM integration).
controls: Structured audit logging framework (JSON/Syslog); NTP time synchronization; log sanitization filters preventing secret leakage; log forwarding to secure SIEM; local log rotation and storage caps.
evidence: Security Logging Architecture & Event Taxonomy; Log Sanitization Verification Test Record; Penetration Test Audit Log Tampering Assessment; User Manual Log Management Guide.
criteria: All security events generate audit logs with accurate timestamps; zero passwords/keys written to logs (verified by SAST); logs exportable via standard formats; local logs protected against unauthorized tampering.
limitations: SonarQube and Coverity detect CWE-117 (Log Injection) and accidental secret logging in source code. Penetration testing tests log evasion and tampering during attack simulations.
additional_controls: SIEM / centralized log forwarding integration; audit log retention policies; user privacy controls for diagnostic logging.
notes: Logs containing personal data must comply with GDPR proportionality while maintaining forensic readiness under CRA and NIS2.

title: Secure Decommissioning & Permanent Data Erasure
description: Products with digital elements shall provide the possibility for users to permanently and securely erase all data and configurations, including any integrated remote data processing solutions, prior to decommissioning or transferring the product.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all products storing user data, credentials, or proprietary configurations)
stakeholder: Product Security Engineer, Firmware Lead, DPO
guidance: Provide an accessible, documented secure data wipe / sanitization routine adhering to NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 or IEEE 2883-2022 standards. The routine must overwrite non-volatile storage, scrub cryptographic keys, revoke cloud session tokens, and de-register associated Remote Data Processing Solutions (RDPS).
controls: Cryptographic erase (crypto-shredding) implementation; NIST SP 800-88 Purge/Clear automation; RDPS cloud tenant de-provisioning API; decommissioning verification checklist.
evidence: Data Sanitization & Decommissioning Architecture; NIST SP 800-88 Data Erasure Verification Test Report; DPIA Data Disposal Sign-off; Customer Decommissioning Guide (Annex II).
criteria: Data erasure permanently destroys cryptographic keys and storage blocks; zero recoverable sensitive data post-wipe; cloud backend associations terminated.
limitations: Automated scanning tools cannot test physical or cryptographic memory sanitization. DPIA establishes erasure compliance; Penetration testing / forensic recovery tests verify absence of residual data.
additional_controls: Cryptographic erasure mechanism; physical flash sanitization testing; customer decommissioning SOP.
notes: Critical for enterprise B2B products being retired, returned, or transferred between commercial entities to prevent residual data leaks.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (1); Art 13(24)
title: Continuous Component Identification & Machine-Readable SBOM
description: Manufacturers shall identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in products with digital elements, including by drawing up a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in a commonly used and machine-readable format, covering at the very least top-level dependencies.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all products containing third-party or open source software)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Lead Software Architect, Release Manager
guidance: Integrate automated SBOM generation into CI/CD build pipelines using standard formats (CycloneDX v1.5/1.6 or SPDX v2.3/v3.0). Capture direct and transitive dependencies, package hashes, licenses, and suppliers. Ingest generated SBOMs into Dependency-Track or Black Duck for continuous post-market vulnerability monitoring.
controls: Automated build-time SBOM generators (cdxgen, syft, Black Duck Detect); continuous SBOM management platform (Dependency-Track); SBOM archive repository; automated delta checking between releases.
evidence: Machine-readable SBOM files (CycloneDX JSON / SPDX XML) for every released build; Dependency-Track component inventory; CI/CD SBOM generation build logs.
criteria: Every production release artifact is accompanied by a cryptographically signed, machine-readable SBOM covering 100% of direct dependencies and known transitives; verified by Dependency-Track / Black Duck.
limitations: SonarQube, Coverity, Nessus, and Pentest do not generate or manage machine-readable SBOMs. Black Duck and Nexus IQ generate SBOMs; Dependency-Track provides dedicated ingestion and continuous lifecycle vulnerability analysis.
additional_controls: Centralized SBOM repository; automated signing of SBOMs (Cosign/Sigstore); market surveillance export procedure.
notes: Under Art 13(24), manufacturers must supply the machine-readable SBOM to national market surveillance authorities upon reasoned request without undue delay.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (2); Art 13(10)
title: Vulnerability Remediation Without Delay via Security Updates
description: In relation to the risks identified, manufacturers shall address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates, and where applicable, automatic security updates.
applicability: Mandatory (Binding operational duty across the entire declared support period)
stakeholder: Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT), Sustaining Engineering Lead
guidance: Establish a formalized PSIRT vulnerability remediation SLA: Critical CVEs triaged within 24 hours, patch released within 7-14 calendar days; High CVEs within 30 days. Maintain backporting capability for supported release branches. Deliver patches as modular, standalone security updates.
controls: PSIRT remediation runbook; automated CVE triage alerts; branch maintenance policies for supported versions; fast-track emergency CI/CD release pipeline.
evidence: PSIRT Ticket Tracking Logs; Vulnerability Triage Records; Emergency Patch Release Notes; Time-to-Remediate (MTTR) Compliance Metrics.
criteria: Documented adherence to vulnerability remediation SLAs; 100% of identified exploitable vulnerabilities addressed via patch or verified workaround within SLA windows.
limitations: Tools detect vulnerabilities; they do not write patches, manage engineering sprints, or execute release pipelines. Nexus IQ and Black Duck provide automated PR guidance; Dependency-Track tracks remediation status.
additional_controls: Dedicated PSIRT team; emergency patch release pipeline; contractual SLA monitoring; engineering backport capacity.
notes: Failure to address known exploitable vulnerabilities without delay constitutes a direct violation of Annex I, Part II, incurring fines under Art 64.

title: Regular Security Testing, Verification & Attack Surface Review
description: Manufacturers shall apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product with digital elements, including during its development and throughout the support period.
applicability: Mandatory (Continuous across development and post-market support phases)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Security QA Lead, Third-Party Pentest Firm
guidance: Establish a multi-layered verification strategy combining automated continuous testing (SAST, SCA, container scanning) in daily CI/CD with periodic deep dynamic testing (DAST) and annual independent third-party penetration testing. Re-test immediately upon significant architectural changes.
controls: CI/CD automated security testing pipelines; scheduled bi-weekly Nessus/Cyberwatch scans; automated DAST regression suites; annual third-party penetration test engagements.
evidence: Annual Penetration Testing Reports; CI/CD Automated Test Execution Logs; DAST Scan Run Logs; Nessus/Cyberwatch Infrastructure Scan Reports.
criteria: All scheduled scans and tests executed according to calendar; zero unaddressed High/Critical findings past remediation SLA; independent test re-validation sign-off.
limitations: No single tool covers all testing dimensions. Full compliance requires an integrated toolchain combining SAST (Coverity/SonarQube), SCA (Black Duck/Nexus), DAST (Burp/ZAP), and manual Penetration Testing.
additional_controls: Annual third-party security audit budget; automated regression testing suites; DevSecOps pipeline orchestrator.
notes: Testing records must be systematically cataloged and retained as part of the Annex VII technical documentation.

title: Public Disclosure of Remediated Vulnerabilities (Security Advisories)
description: Once a security update has been made available, manufacturers shall publicly disclose information about the fixed vulnerabilities, including a description, information on how to obtain the update, and the severity rating.
applicability: Mandatory (Mandatory for all publicly released security patches; timing must coordinate with update availability)
stakeholder: PSIRT Lead, Technical Communications, Legal / Compliance
guidance: Publish standardized security advisories (Common Security Advisory Framework - CSAF 2.0 JSON and human-readable HTML) on a dedicated security portal. Disclose CVE identifier, CVSS v3.1/v4.0 score and vector, affected product versions, remediated versions, and workarounds for unpatched systems.
controls: CSAF advisory authoring pipeline; public security portal (`security.company.com/advisories`); RSS/email alert distribution feed; CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) coordination.
evidence: Published Security Advisories (HTML and CSAF 2.0 JSON); CVE Registry Records; Customer Advisory Email Broadcast Logs.
criteria: Advisory published synchronously with or immediately following patch availability; CSAF format validates against OASIS schema; accurate CVE and CVSS ratings included.
limitations: Vulnerability scanners do not author, review, or publish legal security advisories or operate CSAF advisory portals. Entirely an organizational PSIRT and communications process.
additional_controls: CSAF 2.0 automation toolchain; CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) partnership or coordination; PSIRT advisory review workflow.
notes: Public disclosure must not precede update availability to prevent weaponization against unpatched users, unless coordinated with CSIRTs.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (5); Art 13(19)
title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) Policy
description: Manufacturers shall put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure, aligned with international standards such as ISO/IEC 29147 and ISO/IEC 30111.
applicability: Mandatory (Must be publicly accessible and operational before placing product on market)
stakeholder: CISO, PSIRT Lead, Legal Counsel
guidance: Draft, approve, and publish a formal Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy aligned with ISO/IEC 29147. Specify scope of in-scope products, safe harbor protections for good-faith security researchers, reporting instructions, PGP communication keys, expected triage response times, and disclosure embargo terms.
controls: Formal CVD policy document approved by CISO and Legal; public web page (`/security/disclosure`); PGP key infrastructure; safe harbor legal commitment.
evidence: Published CVD Policy Document; PGP Public Key in Registry; ISO/IEC 29147 Alignment Matrix; Legal Safe Harbor Clause.
criteria: CVD policy accessible publicly without authentication; clear scope and safe harbor terms; valid PGP key published; response timeline commitments defined.
limitations: Zero automated tool coverage. CVD policy is a governance, legal, and operational framework.
additional_controls: CVD Policy Authoring & Legal Review; alignment with ISO/IEC 29147; integration with Bug Bounty / Researcher platforms (HackerOne/Bugcrowd).
notes: CRA explicitly cites CVD as a key mechanism for collaborative security across the Union.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (6); Art 13(19)
title: Public External Vulnerability Reporting Contact Point
description: Manufacturers shall facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities by providing a contact address for the reporting of vulnerabilities discovered in the product with digital elements.
applicability: Mandatory (Single contact point must be active 24/7/365)
stakeholder: PSIRT Lead, Webmaster, Security Operations Lead
guidance: Deploy RFC 9116 compliant `security.txt` file at `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/security.txt` on all public domains. Maintain a dedicated, monitored email intake inbox (`security@company.com`) backed by an encrypted intake form or bug bounty portal. Provide public PGP encryption keys for secure submissions.
controls: RFC 9116 `security.txt` deployment; dedicated PSIRT ticketing queue; 24/7 inbox monitoring with automated acknowledgment; published PGP encryption key.
evidence: RFC 9116 `security.txt` file URL and content; PSIRT Intake Queue Architecture; First-Response SLA Tracking Logs; Published PGP Public Key.
criteria: `security.txt` validates against RFC 9116 schema; submission to `security@` receives automated acknowledgment within 24 hours; researcher reports routed to PSIRT ticketing.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. This is an operational intake channel and communications endpoint.
additional_controls: RFC 9116 `security.txt` web deployment; PSIRT ticketing system integration (Jira Service Desk / ServiceNow); PGP key rotation procedure.
notes: Contact point must be documented in Annex II Instructions for Use supplied with the product.

title: Cryptographically Secured Update Distribution Infrastructure
description: Manufacturers shall ensure that security updates are distributed securely, including by being cryptographically signed, distributed through authentic channels, and protected against manipulation or downgrade attacks.
applicability: Mandatory (All update release channels, binaries, and firmware distribution servers)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Release Manager, Infrastructure Security Lead
guidance: Sign all update packages and binaries using cryptographic keys protected inside hardware security modules (HSM) or cloud KMS (Sigstore / Cosign). Enforce signature verification on client devices prior to installation. Distribute updates over TLS-only CDN channels with mutual TLS or strict certificate pinning. Implement anti-rollback / anti-downgrade monotonic version checks.
controls: HSM-backed automated code signing in CI/CD; client-side cryptographic signature verification daemon; TLS 1.3 update repository; monotonic counter anti-rollback enforcement.
evidence: Code Signing Architecture & Key Custody Procedure; Client Signature Verification Code Review / Unit Tests; Anti-Downgrade Test Record; Penetration Test Update Tampering Assessment.
criteria: Client device strictly rejects unsigned, modified, or expired update binaries; downgrade to older vulnerable version is rejected; signing keys secured in HSM with split-custody access.
limitations: Scanners cannot evaluate PKI signing ceremonies or client verification logic. Penetration testing tests client signature verification bypasses and man-in-the-middle tampering.
additional_controls: HSM Key Management infrastructure; update distribution CDN hardening; anti-rollback firmware fuses/counters.
notes: Failure in update security can compromise the entire fleet simultaneously, making this a top priority during conformity assessment.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (8); Art 13(10)
title: Free-of-Charge Security Updates & Feature Decoupling
description: Manufacturers shall ensure that security updates are made available free of charge throughout the support period, and that security updates are separated from functional updates where technically feasible.
applicability: Mandatory (Default); Conditional (Narrow contractual waiver permitted for bespoke tailor-made B2B software under Recital 64)
stakeholder: Product Manager, Finance Director, Legal Counsel, Software Architect
guidance: Structure commercial software contracts and pricing models to guarantee free security patches for the full duration of the declared support period. Decouple security patches from commercial feature upgrades in Git branches and release artifacts, enabling users to patch without being forced to license new features.
controls: Dual-track release branching strategy (LTS security-only branch vs main feature branch); commercial contract terms template; public update repository with unrestricted access for security patches.
evidence: Release Branching Architecture Spec; Standard Commercial Terms & Conditions (CRA Free Update Guarantee); Multi-Year Software Maintenance Financial Model.
criteria: Security patches compile and deploy independently of paid feature releases; customers can download security patches without subscription renewal or paywall.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Entirely a commercial, architectural, and contractual obligation.
additional_controls: Software release branching policy; commercial contract review; long-term engineering maintenance funding.
notes: Recital 64 permits custom enterprise software agreements to explicitly negotiate bespoke commercial maintenance terms, provided this is documented in writing.

title: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Across Full Product Lifecycle
description: Manufacturers shall undertake an assessment of the cybersecurity risks associated with a product with digital elements and take the outcome of that assessment into account during the planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance phases, including risks from third-party components.
applicability: Mandatory (Mandatory statutory prerequisite for Technical Documentation Annex VII and CE marking)
stakeholder: Lead Security Architect, CISO, Product Manager
guidance: Execute structured Threat Analysis and Risk Analysis (TARA) using STRIDE, PASTA, ISO/IEC 27005, or IEC 62443-4-1 methodologies. Identify operational assets, threat actors, attack surfaces, and third-party dependencies. Document technical and organizational mitigations. Re-evaluate and update the risk assessment at every major release and during post-market maintenance.
controls: Organizational Risk Assessment Standard; Threat Modeling Software / Templates; Living Cybersecurity Risk Register; annual risk assessment re-certification gate.
evidence: Formal Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Document (Annex VII dossier element); Threat Model Architecture Schemas; Residual Risk Acceptance Sign-off; Third-Party Risk Analysis Appendices.
criteria: Risk assessment covers 100% of functional components and external data interfaces; all High/Critical risks mitigated to acceptable levels; formal annual sign-off by CISO.
limitations: Scanning tools test code syntax and known signatures; they cannot conduct high-level risk assessments. TARA is the dedicated engineering process. Penetration testing supplies empirical validation data.
additional_controls: Living Threat Modeling Program; Risk Assessment Methodology standard; Executive Risk Governance Board.
notes: Failure to produce an up-to-date Cybersecurity Risk Assessment invalidates the Annex VII Technical Documentation and exposes the manufacturer to market withdrawal.

title: Due Diligence & Security Screening of Third-Party & Open Source Components
description: When integrating components sourced from third parties, including open-source software, manufacturers shall exercise due diligence to ensure that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product with digital elements.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all integrated commercial COTS, third-party libraries, and open-source packages)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Procurement Manager, Software Architect
guidance: Establish open-source and third-party component selection policies: evaluate repository maintenance health (OpenSSF Scorecard, commit frequency, active maintainers, vulnerability response history), verify license compliance, screen for known vulnerabilities before ingestion, and enforce automated SCA gating in CI/CD.
controls: Enterprise Open Source Software (OSS) Ingestion Policy; automated SCA pre-merge pull-request gating; internal curated package repository (Artifactory / Nexus Repository); vendor security evaluation questionnaires.
evidence: Third-Party Component Due Diligence Procedure; Black Duck / Nexus IQ Ingestion Scan Records; OpenSSF Scorecard Audit Logs; Approved Component Whitelist.
criteria: Zero unvetted third-party components merged into production builds; all dependencies pass automated SCA security quality gates; high-risk/abandoned libraries rejected.
limitations: SAST scanners and pentesting do not assess supplier due diligence or package hygiene. Nexus IQ Lifecycle and Black Duck provide the core SCA engines for vetting open-source health, licenses, and CVEs.
additional_controls: Curated internal artifact repository; procurement vendor assessment checklist; OpenSSF Scorecard automation.
notes: Manufacturers retain full legal product liability under CRA even when the vulnerability originates in an unmaintained open-source library.

title: Mandatory Reporting of Vulnerabilities in Upstream Components
description: Manufacturers shall, upon identifying a vulnerability in a component, including in an open-source component, integrated in the product with digital elements, report the vulnerability to the person or entity maintaining the component, and address and remediate it.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory duty whenever internal security testing discovers a zero-day or unpatched flaw in an upstream component)
stakeholder: PSIRT Lead, DevSecOps Lead, Open Source Program Office (OSPO)
guidance: Establish a formalized Upstream Vulnerability Disclosure SOP: when internal testing (fuzzing, code review, pentest) finds a previously undisclosed vulnerability in an upstream COTS or OSS library, responsibly notify the upstream maintainer via their CVD channel, share proof-of-concept and proposed patches, and coordinate public disclosure.
controls: Upstream Disclosure Operating Procedure; secure PGP communication channels; patch contribution workflow; tracking log of upstream outreach tickets.
evidence: Upstream Vulnerability Disclosure Notifications; GitHub Security Advisory / Email Transmission Records; Upstream Pull Request / Patch Contributions; PSIRT Disclosure Audit Log.
criteria: All internally discovered third-party vulnerabilities reported to upstream maintainer within 5 business days; proof of outreach recorded in PSIRT audit trail.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Tools may identify the bug, but executing responsible upstream disclosure is an organizational and community engagement process.
additional_controls: Upstream Vulnerability Disclosure SOP; OSPO coordination; secure researcher communication channels.
notes: Crucial community reciprocity mechanism designed to improve the collective cybersecurity baseline of the open-source ecosystem.

title: Post-Market Vulnerability Monitoring & Continuous Handling Program
description: Manufacturers shall systematically document and handle vulnerabilities throughout the support period, investigating reports, maintaining records, and updating their cybersecurity risk assessment accordingly.
applicability: Mandatory (Continuous statutory duty lasting for the entire declared support period of every product placed on the market)
stakeholder: CISO, PSIRT Lead, Security Operations Manager
guidance: Deploy an automated, continuous post-market vulnerability monitoring system. Ingest production SBOMs into Dependency-Track or Black Duck to continuously correlate deployed component inventories against newly published CVEs from NVD, OSV, and security advisories. Route new alerts to PSIRT triage queues.
controls: Continuous SBOM correlation engine (Dependency-Track / Black Duck); 24/7 NVD/OSV feed synchronization; automated Jira/ServiceNow ticket creation; weekly PSIRT vulnerability triage review.
evidence: Continuous Vulnerability Monitoring Platform Audit Logs; PSIRT Weekly Triage Minutes; Vulnerability Ingestion & Resolution Metrics Dashboard; Updated Risk Assessment Addenda.
criteria: 100% of released product versions actively monitored; newly published CVEs matching product SBOM alerted within 24 hours of NVD/OSV disclosure; triage initiated immediately.
limitations: Code-level SAST does not monitor deployed production fleets. Dependency-Track and Black Duck provide dedicated continuous post-release SBOM monitoring; Nessus/Cyberwatch monitors live infrastructure.
additional_controls: Standing PSIRT operations team; threat intelligence feed integration; quarterly post-market risk review cadence.
notes: Applies across all active customer installations and historical versions that remain within their declared support period.

title: Guaranteed Security Support Period Determination & Communication
description: Manufacturers shall determine and explicitly state the support period during which vulnerabilities will be handled effectively, taking into account user expectations and product lifetime (at least 5 years unless a shorter period is justified by the product's nature).
applicability: Mandatory (Support period must be contractually and publicly stated prior to placing product on market)
stakeholder: Product Management VP, Business Unit Director, Legal Counsel, Finance Lead
guidance: Establish a formal methodology to calculate product support lifetime. The statutory baseline is at least 5 years from placing on the market unless an explicitly shorter expected lifetime (e.g. 2-year disposable IoT sensor) is objectively justified and documented. Disclose exact end-of-support date on public website, marketing materials, and Annex II documentation.
controls: Executive Support Period Governance Policy; multi-year engineering maintenance cost model; public support lifecycle web portal (`company.com/lifecycle`); Annex II datasheet disclosure template.
evidence: Formal Support Period Determination Record; Multi-Year Sustaining Engineering Budget Model; Public End-of-Support Disclosure Web Page; Annex II User Instructions Statement.
criteria: Support period documented in Annex VII dossier and Annex II user instructions; minimum 5 years guaranteed unless shorter period formally justified and approved by Legal; public disclosure accessible.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Support period determination is an executive business, financial, and legal commitment requiring multi-year resource provisioning.
additional_controls: Support period financial provisioning; executive governance approval gate; public product lifecycle registry.
notes: Under Commission Guidance C(2026) 5252, stating 'supported until further notice' is strictly non-compliant; an explicit calendar date or definitive calculation rule is required.

title: Mandatory 10-Year Retention of Released Security Updates in Public Archive
description: Manufacturers shall ensure that each security update made available during the support period remains available for at least 10 years after the product has been placed on the market, or for the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory IT archiving and repository retention duty)
stakeholder: Release Engineering Lead, DevOps Infrastructure Lead, Legal Counsel
guidance: Establish an immutable, long-term binary archive repository (e.g., S3 Glacier / Artifactory cold storage) retaining all compiled security updates, patches, firmware images, and associated release notes. Ensure public or customer accessibility for at least 10 years following initial market placement.
controls: Immutable cloud storage bucket with WORM (Write Once, Read Many) policies; automated post-release archiving pipeline; public patch archive index; retention policy audit automation.
evidence: Long-Term Update Archive Architecture Specification; Cloud Immutable Storage Policy Verification; Patch Archive Directory Listing & Health Check Report; 10-Year Retention Compliance Record.
criteria: All historical security updates downloadable and integrity-verified via SHA-256 hashes; deletion or alteration blocked by cloud WORM retention lock for 10 years.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Dedicated DevOps and infrastructure archiving obligation.
additional_controls: WORM-compliant binary storage; automated backup and escrow procedures; long-term domain and CDN maintenance plan.
notes: Ensures that users operating products across their operational lifecycles retain access to critical security remediation patches.

title: Single-Version Patching Governance & Free Customer Upgrade Paths
description: Where a manufacturer applies security updates only to the latest version of the product, it shall ensure that customers can easily and free of charge upgrade to that version throughout the support period.
applicability: Conditional (Applies when engineering strategy opts NOT to backport security patches to older minor/major versions)
stakeholder: Lead Software Architect, Product Management VP, Release Engineering Lead
guidance: If the organization decides not to backport security patches across multiple historical branches, it must guarantee that upgrading to the patched latest version is seamless, non-breaking, automated, and free of charge. Breaking changes or paid license upgrades cannot block access to security fixes.
controls: Automated migration scripts / backward-compatible schema evolutions; free upgrade licensing terms; automated compatibility test suites across major upgrade jumps.
evidence: Single-Version Maintenance Strategy Policy; Automated Upgrade & Database Migration Test Reports; Zero-Cost License Upgrade Verification; Customer Release Communications.
criteria: Automated upgrade from any supported version to latest version succeeds without manual intervention or data loss; zero commercial licensing fees required to access security fixes.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Software release architecture, migration engineering, and commercial licensing governance.
additional_controls: Backward-compatibility automated testing suite; smooth migration path engineering; contractual free upgrade guarantee.
notes: Prevents manufacturers from forcing customers to pay for new software features or major version upgrades just to obtain critical security patches.

title: Technical Documentation Dossier Compilation Prior to Market Placement
description: Manufacturers shall draw up the technical documentation containing all relevant data or details of the means used by the manufacturer to ensure that the product with digital elements complies with the essential requirements set out in Annex I.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory prerequisite for CE marking and market placement under Art 31 and Annex VII)
stakeholder: Regulatory Compliance Lead, Product Security Architect, Lead Systems Engineer
guidance: Assemble a comprehensive Technical Documentation Dossier meeting Annex VII requirements: product overview, system architecture diagrams, cybersecurity risk assessment report, design specifications, SBOM, test verification records (SAST, SCA, DAST, pentest), user instructions (Annex II), and EU Declaration of Conformity.
controls: Annex VII Documentation Management System; automated compilation of CI/CD scan artifacts; formal Technical Dossier Review and Approval Gate prior to release.
evidence: Completed Annex VII Technical Documentation Dossier; System Architecture Diagrams; Risk Assessment Dossier; Security Verification Test Dossier; Bill of Materials Dossier.
criteria: Dossier contains all 11 mandatory elements specified in Annex VII; formally approved and signed by Chief Engineer and Compliance Officer prior to commercial release.
limitations: Tools generate raw scan reports and data feeds that serve as evidence attachments; the compilation, structuring, and authoring of the Annex VII technical dossier is a human governance process.
additional_controls: Technical Dossier Authoring Standard; Annex VII Compliance Checklist; Executive Engineering Sign-off Gate.
notes: Must be made available to national market surveillance authorities within 10 days of a reasoned request in an official Union language.

title: 10-Year Retention of Technical Documentation Dossier and EU DoC
description: Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the product has been placed on the market, or for the support period, whichever is longer.
applicability: Mandatory (Mandatory statutory records retention obligation)
stakeholder: Compliance Officer, Legal Counsel, Corporate Records Archivist
guidance: Store all versions of the Annex VII technical documentation, test reports, and signed EU Declarations of Conformity in a secure, tamper-evident corporate compliance archive. Implement strict 10-year retention policies, disaster recovery backups, and designated custodian roles.
controls: Enterprise Compliance Document Management System; immutable legal hold archiving; annual archive integrity audits; designated regulatory record keeper.
evidence: Compliance Archive Access Log; 10-Year Retention Policy Document; Archival Verification Audit Trail; Signed DoC Repository Index.
criteria: Dossiers for all placed products indexed, searchable, and retrievable within 24 hours; records protected against deletion for minimum 10 years from market placement.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Corporate legal records management and archiving duty.
additional_controls: Enterprise Records Management System; legal retention schedules; regulatory audit readiness runbook.
notes: Even if the product line is discontinued, the retention duty remains legally binding on the legal entity.

title: Customer Technical Security Information & Instructions for Use
description: Manufacturers shall provide the information and instructions for use set out in Annex II with the product with digital elements, in paper or electronic form, ensuring that users are informed of security parameters, secure installation, support period, and CVD contact.
applicability: Mandatory (Must accompany the product at delivery in official Union language(s) required by Member States)
stakeholder: Lead Technical Writer, Product Security Architect, Product Manager
guidance: Author and publish the Annex II User Security Guide: product intended use, cybersecurity properties, hardware/software requirements, secure installation and hardening instructions, default passwords policy, update configuration, explicit end-of-support date, and single contact point for vulnerability reporting.
controls: Annex II Documentation Authoring Checklist; technical review gate by Product Security Architect; customer documentation publishing workflow; multi-language translation management.
evidence: Published User Manual & Security Guide (Annex II Dossier); Online Documentation Portal URL; Packaging Quick-Start Security Leaflet; Translation Certification Records.
criteria: User documentation includes all 9 mandatory points from Annex II; clearly specifies support period end date and CVD contact point; available in required Member State languages.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Technical writing, product security communications, and customer documentation process.
additional_controls: Annex II Compliance Checklist; technical writing review gate; customer documentation portal.
notes: Electronic format is permitted, but must be easily accessible to the user and maintained online throughout the product support period.

title: Cooperation with Market Surveillance Authorities & SBOM Provisioning
description: Manufacturers shall, upon a reasoned request from a market surveillance authority, provide that authority with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity, and provide the machine-readable SBOM.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory regulatory inspection cooperation duty)
stakeholder: Legal Counsel, Chief Compliance Officer, PSIRT Lead
guidance: Establish a Market Surveillance Authority Response Procedure: designate point of contact, define workflow to retrieve Annex VII dossier, test reports, and generate machine-readable SBOM within statutory response window (typically 10-15 business days). Maintain confidentiality protocols for proprietary code disclosures.
controls: Market Surveillance Interaction SOP; designated Single Point of Contact (SPOC); automated SBOM export pipeline from Dependency-Track / Black Duck; executive response escalation path.
evidence: Market Surveillance Response Operating Procedure; Designated Authority Contact Record; Test Drill SBOM Export Logs; Authority Request Tracking Register.
criteria: Procedure tested via annual drill; ability to produce complete Annex VII dossier and validated machine-readable SBOM within 5 business days of request.
limitations: Dependency-Track and Black Duck can export the machine-readable SBOM in CycloneDX/SPDX format. The formal interaction and legal defense is a legal/compliance function.
additional_controls: Market Surveillance Response Runbook; legal escalation tree; authority inquiry drill.
notes: Failure to cooperate with market surveillance authorities can trigger administrative fines under Art 64(3) up to €10,000,000 or 2% of turnover.

ref: Art 7, Art 8, Art 32; Annexes III, IV; IR (EU) 2025/2392
title: Product Classification & Conformity Assessment Route Selection
description: Manufacturers shall classify the product with digital elements into the Default, Important Class I, Important Class II, or Critical category, and execute the corresponding conformity assessment procedure (Module A, Module B+C, Module H, or European Cybersecurity Certification).
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory requirement determining conformity route and Notified Body engagement)
stakeholder: Lead Product Architect, Regulatory Compliance Officer, Legal Counsel
guidance: Assess product core functionality against Annex III and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392: Default products use Module A (Internal Control); Important Class I uses Module A (if harmonised standards applied) or Module B+C / Module H; Important Class II requires mandatory Notified Body assessment (Module B+C or Module H); Critical products under Annex IV may require EUCC certification.
controls: Product Classification Decision Matrix; early Notified Body engagement procedure (if Class I/II); conformity assessment project plan.
evidence: Formal Product Classification Record; Conformity Assessment Strategy Document; Notified Body Engagement Agreement / Quotation (if Class I/II); Internal Control Plan (Module A).
criteria: Classification verified against IR 2025/2392; correct conformity route selected; if Class I/II, Notified Body engagement scheduled 6+ months ahead of release.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Strategic product classification and regulatory assessment process.
additional_controls: CRA Product Classification Checklist; legal review of intended use and marketing claims; Notified Body procurement process.
notes: Marketing claims must align strictly with assessed intended use; claiming security functionality (e.g. firewall/IAM) may unintentionally escalate product into Important Class I/II.

title: Execution & Signing of the EU Declaration of Conformity
description: The manufacturer shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity stating that the fulfilment of the applicable essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I has been demonstrated.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory legal instrument required before CE mark can be affixed or product placed on market)
stakeholder: Managing Director / CEO, VP Engineering, Regulatory Affairs Lead
guidance: Draft the EU Declaration of Conformity strictly adhering to Annex V: product identification (name, type, batch/serial number), manufacturer details, statement of sole responsibility, conformity assessment module applied, references to relevant harmonised standards or common specifications, Notified Body certificate details (if applicable), and authorized executive signature.
controls: EU Declaration of Conformity authoring workflow; executive signature authorization matrix; DoC repository management; customer delivery bundling.
evidence: Signed EU Declaration of Conformity (PDF / Annex V Dossier); Executive Board Resolution Authorizing Signatory; Harmonised Standards / Specification Mapping Record.
criteria: DoC contains all 8 mandatory fields from Annex V; signed by duly authorized corporate officer; verified alignment with technical documentation dossier.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Formal legal instrument executed by executive management.
additional_controls: Executive Signatory Authorization SOP; DoC verification checklist; multi-directive bundling review (e.g. RED / Machinery / CRA).
notes: Signing the DoC establishes full legal responsibility for product cybersecurity conformity under Union law.

title: Affixing the CE Marking, Identification & Traceability Markings
description: Manufacturers shall affix the CE marking visibly, legibly and indelibly to the product with digital elements, or where that is not possible, to its packaging or accompanying documents, along with manufacturer identification and traceability details.
applicability: Mandatory (Mandatory physical or digital marking condition for placing on Union market)
stakeholder: Hardware Packaging Lead, Product Release Manager, Compliance Officer
guidance: Apply CE marking adhering to Article 30 proportions (minimum 5mm height). For hardware: affix to device body, rating plate, or packaging. For standalone software: display CE mark in the 'About' box, CLI splash screen, e-label, or accompanying digital datasheet. Include manufacturer postal address, website, email, and product model/batch/serial number.
controls: Packaging and artwork approval gate; software UI 'About' screen verification; digital labelling guidelines compliance check; hardware label durability testing.
evidence: Approved Packaging Artwork & Rating Plate Proofs; Software UI 'About' Screen Screenshot Archive; Hardware Label Durability Test Report; Marking Compliance Verification Sign-off.
criteria: CE marking visibly affixed according to statutory dimensions; manufacturer identification and contact details legible; software UI displays CE mark and version traceability.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Physical artwork, packaging design, and software UI release governance.
additional_controls: Artwork approval workflow; UI digital labelling verification; packaging inspection prior to factory dispatch.
notes: If a Notified Body participated in production control (Module H), its 4-digit identification number must follow the CE mark.

title: Substantial Modification Change Management & Gating Governance
description: Any modification to a product with digital elements following its placing on the market which affects compliance with Annex I or modifies the intended purpose constitutes a substantial modification, requiring a new conformity assessment and new placing on the market.
applicability: Mandatory (Change control gate governing all post-release functional updates and architectural refactors)
stakeholder: Lead Security Architect, Change Advisory Board (CAB) Chair, Compliance Officer
guidance: Implement a formal Substantial Modification Gating Filter in the engineering Change Advisory Board (CAB): evaluate whether planned feature updates introduce new attack vectors, alter trust boundaries, change cryptographic primitives, or modify intended use. If substantial, execute a new conformity assessment, update Annex VII dossier, and issue a new EU DoC.
controls: Substantial Modification Assessment Checklist; CAB regulatory screening gate; architectural delta review board; change ticketing integration (Jira CAB workflow).
evidence: Substantial Modification Screening Records for each major release; CAB Approval Minutes; Updated Annex VII Dossier Addenda; Updated EU Declaration of Conformity (if triggered).
criteria: 100% of major software releases and feature updates screened against Art 3(30) criteria; non-substantial changes documented; substantial modifications routed to new conformity assessment.
limitations: Automated tools cannot evaluate legal substantial modification thresholds. TARA supplies the comparative risk profile analysis. Governance is enforced by the CAB.
additional_controls: Engineering CAB Regulatory Gating Filter; Architectural Delta Analysis SOP; legal re-certification checklist.
notes: Routine security patches and minor bug fixes that do not increase the risk profile do NOT constitute substantial modifications (Guidance C(2026) 5252 Pt 15).

title: Statutory Multi-Stage Reporting of Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities
description: Manufacturers shall notify any actively exploited vulnerability contained in the product with digital elements to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and to ENISA via the Single Reporting Platform within strict statutory deadlines: 24h Early Warning, 72h Detailed Notification, and 14-day Final Report.
applicability: Mandatory (LIVE STATUTORY LAW since 11 September 2026; applies retroactively to all products made available on Union market)
stakeholder: CISO, PSIRT Incident Commander, Legal Counsel
guidance: Operationalize the Article 14 Reporting Runbook: establish 24/7/365 PSIRT awareness monitoring; configure access to ENISA Single Reporting Platform (SRP - portal.cra-srp.enisa.europa.eu) via EU Login / FIDO2; execute statutory notification clock upon becoming aware of active exploitation (24h early warning, 72h detailed notification, 14-day final report). Request delayed dissemination under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/881 if disclosure creates imminent exploitation risk.
controls: Article 14 Operational Runbook; ENISA SRP accounts with primary/secondary representatives; 24/7 PSIRT incident escalation tree; emergency template repository; CSIRT coordinator hotline directory.
evidence: ENISA SRP Submission Confirmation Receipts; PSIRT Incident Awareness Timestamp Logs; 24h Early Warning Records; 72h Notification Dossiers; 14-Day Final Technical Reports.
criteria: 100% of confirmed actively exploited vulnerabilities reported within 24h of awareness; detailed technical report submitted within 72h; final report submitted within 14 days or upon patch availability.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Statutory regulatory reporting obligation enforced via European cybersecurity authorities. Tools may identify the bug, but cannot execute legal ENISA SRP filings.
additional_controls: Live Article 14 Incident Response Runbook; bi-annual simulated reporting drills; 24/7 legal escalation roster; ENISA SRP credential custody.
notes: LIVE RIGHT NOW (enforceable since 11 September 2026). Violations incur fines under Art 64(2) of up to €15,000,000 or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover.

title: Statutory Multi-Stage Reporting of Severe Product Security Incidents
description: Manufacturers shall notify any severe incident having an impact on the security of the product with digital elements to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and to ENISA via the Single Reporting Platform: 24h Early Warning, 72h Incident Notification, and 1-month Final Report.
applicability: Mandatory (LIVE STATUTORY LAW since 11 September 2026; covers incidents compromising product availability, integrity, or delivery infrastructure)
stakeholder: CISO, Head of Security Operations, Legal Counsel
guidance: Integrate CRA severe incident reporting into corporate SOC/CSIRT workflows: identify incidents impacting PDE security (e.g., compromise of build pipeline, code-signing key theft, malicious supply chain injection, disruption of update infrastructure, active remote exploitation causing material harm). Submit 24h Early Warning, 72h Detailed Notification, and 1-Month Final Comprehensive Report via ENISA SRP.
controls: SOC Severe Incident Identification Matrix; automated ENISA SRP notification workflow; bridge protocol linking NIS2 incident response with CRA Article 14 reporting; executive crisis management team.
evidence: ENISA SRP Incident Notification Receipts; SOC Incident Severity Triage Logs; 24h Early Warning Records; 72h Detailed Notification Reports; 1-Month Final Incident Root-Cause Dossiers.
criteria: Statutory deadlines strictly met (24h early warning, 72h notification, 1-month final report); root-cause analysis and remediation roadmap formally documented.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Statutory CSIRT/ENISA incident notification procedure requiring legal and operational coordination.
additional_controls: Article 14 Severe Incident Runbook; SOC severity classification playbooks; tabletop incident simulation exercises.
notes: Applies when the incident impacts the security of the product itself or the infrastructure used to develop, build, sign, or distribute updates.

ref: Art 14(8); Annex I, Part II, point (4)
title: Mandatory Timely Notification of Affected Users Regarding Exploits/Incidents
description: Where necessary, manufacturers shall inform affected users of the actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident without undue delay and, where relevant, of any risk-mitigation measures that users can take.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies whenever active exploitation or a severe incident threatens user environments)
stakeholder: CISO, VP Customer Success, Communications Lead, Legal Counsel
guidance: Establish a customer emergency advisory mechanism: upon confirming active exploitation or a severe security incident, disseminate clear actionable advisory notices to affected users without undue delay via direct email, in-app notifications, customer portal alerts, and public advisories. Provide interim mitigation steps, configuration workarounds, and update instructions.
controls: Customer Security Advisory Broadcast Platform; emergency customer contact registry; pre-approved customer communication templates; dedicated customer response hotline/portal.
evidence: Customer Emergency Advisory Broadcast Logs; Published Mitigation Bulletins; Customer Response / Ticket Resolution Metrics; In-App Alert Broadcast Audit Records.
criteria: Customer advisories dispatched without undue delay; clear actionable technical workarounds provided; verified receipt by designated customer security contacts.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Customer communications, crisis management, and external customer support process.
additional_controls: Customer Emergency Advisory Runbook; customer contact database maintenance; automated advisory dispatch tool.
notes: Timing of user notification should coordinate with patch availability or immediate mitigation guidance to avoid creating unmitigated exposure.

title: Non-Conformity Corrective Actions, Market Surveillance & Product Recall
description: Manufacturers who consider or have reason to believe that a product with digital elements is not in conformity with this Regulation shall immediately take the corrective measures necessary to bring that product into conformity, to withdraw it or to recall it, and inform market surveillance authorities.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory product safety compliance and corrective measure mechanism)
stakeholder: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Product Quality, Legal Counsel
guidance: Establish a formal Product Non-Conformity & Recall Procedure: upon identifying non-conformity (e.g. invalid CE mark, unmitigated critical design defect, missing essential requirement), initiate root-cause investigation, determine whether to issue emergency software update, withdraw product from distribution, or initiate customer recall. Notify competent national market surveillance authorities immediately.
controls: Product Non-Conformity SOP; Executive Product Safety Committee; automated distribution quarantine controls; market surveillance authority notification templates.
evidence: Non-Conformity Incident Investigation Reports; Executive Corrective Action Decision Records; Market Surveillance Authority Notifications; Product Withdrawal / Quarantine Logs.
criteria: Corrective action plan initiated within 48 hours of confirmed non-conformity; national market surveillance authorities notified where serious risk exists; product distribution halted if non-compliant.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Executive product safety, quality assurance, and legal regulatory governance.
additional_controls: Product Safety & Recall SOP; distribution quarantine mechanism; regulatory authority notification runbook.
notes: Covers both technical cybersecurity non-conformities and formal administrative non-conformities (e.g., defective CE marking, missing DoC).

title: Advance Statutory Notification of Corporate Cessation or Product Retirement
description: Manufacturers shall, where they cease their operations or the commercial activity related to the product with digital elements, inform the market surveillance authorities concerned and users in advance.
applicability: Mandatory (Statutory obligation in the event of corporate restructuring, bankruptcy, or product line discontinuation)
stakeholder: Executive Board, General Counsel, VP Product Management
guidance: Establish a Corporate Cessation & Product Retirement Protocol: if terminating product line or entering insolvency/restructuring, issue formal advance notification to market surveillance authorities and affected customers. Provide clear information regarding remaining support options, open-sourcing of codebase, code escrow release, or migration recommendations.
controls: Product Retirement & End-of-Life (EOL) Policy; corporate wind-down legal runbook; code escrow agreements for critical enterprise clients; authority notification register.
evidence: Advance Product Discontinuation Notices; Market Surveillance Authority Communications; Code Escrow Release Records; Customer Retirement Advisory Transmissions.
criteria: Formal advance notice delivered to authorities and customers at least 6 months prior to cessation of vulnerability handling; escrow or alternative maintenance paths executed.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Executive corporate governance, legal affairs, and commercial lifecycle management.
additional_controls: Software Escrow Policy; Customer EOL Transition Plan; Regulatory Wind-Down Procedure.
notes: Prevents manufacturers from abruptly abandoning products with digital elements without giving customers time to migrate or secure their environments.

title: Supply Chain Due Diligence, Importer Verification & Distributor Compliance
description: Economic operators across the supply chain (importers and distributors) shall verify that the manufacturer has carried out the conformity assessment, drawn up technical documentation, affixed the CE marking, and provided user instructions before making products available.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all distribution channels, value-added resellers, importers, and procurement agreements)
stakeholder: Supply Chain Director, Procurement Lead, Partner Operations Manager
guidance: Establish supply chain verification controls across all distribution channels: verify that hardware/software partners hold valid CE marks, complete Annex VII dossiers, signed EU Declarations of Conformity, and compliant Annex II user instructions. Contractually bind distributors not to alter product security parameters or supply non-compliant units.
controls: Partner Compliance Verification Checklist; distributor contract addenda (CRA compliance clauses); inbound shipment CE mark inspections; distributor training program.
evidence: Distributor & Importer Compliance Audit Records; Inbound Product Inspection Logs; Executed Partner Master Services Agreement CRA Addenda; Distributor Verification Registry.
criteria: 100% of commercial distribution partners bound by CRA compliance terms; zero third-party products distributed without verified CE mark and EU DoC.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Commercial contract management, supply chain governance, and channel partner oversight.
additional_controls: CRA Commercial Partner Addendum; channel distribution auditing; inbound quality control inspection SOP.
notes: If an importer or distributor modifies a product or markets it under their own brand, they legally become the manufacturer under Art 21 or 22.
